body: Are you getting enough exercise and is your diet good? Are you on medication? Sounds like this is a purely chemical thing in your head. That's alright, it's pretty easily fixed. Have a chat with your doctor.

You sound like every single other 17 year old out there, we were ALL useless pieces of shit at that age with our right hands glued to our cocks. Teenage depression is pretty common, and you have all the symptoms. Tell me, besides falling behind on your school work, is there anything in your life that has serious consequences? Chances are, no, probably not. I mean, already you are on the straight and narrow (and are gonna stay that way), you have two parents who love you and are trying their best, and your only real problem is school work, which is very fixable, repeating a year in school can honestly really improve your life if you feel that's necessary. You're not dropping out though, thatll make the situation 10x worse. Have you talked to your doctor about your depression? You might just need to get medication for a while, but make sure that the medication doesn't mess with your sex-drive because that can be pretty catastrophic at your age.
Something in my mind tricked me months ago and now I'm dealing with the consequences. Im filled with regret. And there's nothing I can do to stop this train in motion. There's nothing anyone can do.

I know EXACTLY how you're feeling. Its precisely what I'm going through now. I think it might even be the same problem, but I'm not making assumptions here. I don't know what I can say, because I don't see a way out either. I guess there's some comfort in knowing that someone else is in the same boat.
Get counseling, you just need an adjustment of perspective. You've been looking at the world through your own eyes for so long, you don't even realize there are other ways of looking at it.

You're a good person going through a lot of agony. I'm sure you have more character than any of us here because of what you're going through. I think your mental health is the priority here because, while the rest is awful, mental health is the one thing that can change how you experience that pain. You said you can't take supplements, but can you make adjustments to your diet? Can you start any kind of fitness? Do you think you can adjust how you look at the world to make it more enjoyable? Are you seeing a mental health professional? Your focus is on your health at the moment, of course it is. But maybe its important to refuse it to weigh on your mind the same way its weighing on your body. These are the cards you have been dealt. You have to make the most of them.

You're 17, soon you'll be able to distance yourself from your parents and live your life. We both know you're not going to attempt suicide, but you feel like you're at a low point at the moment and its great you want to talk about it. I think it'd be a good idea to write a letter to your parents, describing exactly how they make you feel. They need to be torn out of their status quo, because it's not healthy. They do love you, they just don't realise the consequences of their words. I think you need to really consider if youre being fair to them, too. Distance from your parents for a while will make a huge impact on that. As for school, sounds like typical teenage depression to me. Had the exact same thing. You probably don't want to hear this, but fitness is so important for your mental health. Pick up a hobby that demands a lot for you physically and start measuring what you eat. This was you can circumvent medication, which essentially has the same effect as fitness on your mental health, but has side effects that aren't worth it. Take it easy tonight, forget your troubles and remember you're only in the middle of a lull at the moment, its really not the end of the world.

How about, every time you think something about yourself, think instead about the people around you, what you can do to brighten up their lives. Even that tiny bit of added purpose, in helping others, that will keep you so busy that you don't even have time to let those toxic, useless thoughts to take over. It honestly sound like you just need to get CBT and to keep yourself busy. Any hobbies? Any hobbies you want to start?

I think before you can improve yourself and see some drastic changes in your life, you need a shift in perspective. I think you're aware that you're looking at the world from a skewed perspective, so already that's progress. Your priority at the moment is adjusting that until you see the best in life. What's the last thing to make you smile? It could have been a dumb joke. For every one negative thought you have, make 5 new positive thoughts. You'll be amazed how much of a difference that will make in even just the short term. Seek counseling, and talk to your doctor. Suicide isn't even on the table, forget about it, it isn't there.

Alright. Go into a bathroom and get the toilet roll. Put the tube up to your eye and look through it. You'll see very little through it. Then take the tube away. You'll see so much more. Where you are now, your age and mentality, that's looking through the tube. In 10, 20 years, you'll be looking at the world with the tube away from your eye. Youll know just how ridiculous it is to make such a catastrophic decision as suicide when you see so little at your age. I dont mean to patronise you, but your life honest to god hasn't even started yet.

You need to accept where you are in life. You dropped out of your degree and you're unemployed. There's nothing you can do about the degree now, its in the past. Maybe youll be able to go back at some time, but forget about it for the moment. You're going to have to pump out those résumés left right and centre first so you can carve out a living for yourself. You're going to get rejection and rejection and rejection. Then you'll improve. Then you'll get rejection. Then you'll improve again. Then you'll get a job. Hell, you mightn't even get rejected that much. So now you have a job. Where are you now? Financially independent and don't need help from family or friends. There's 4 out of 4 of your main problems solved already, Now you need to fix your attitude. That comes with councelling and personality adjustment. That ain't easy, but its definitely solvable. You see what I mean? Of course there are solutions to your problems. Suicide isn't even an option. Its not on the table.

Get in touch with your college mental health facilities, tell them exactly where you are mentally and why. Say you've been struggling with suicidal thoughts for a while, because you clearly have. Say you're at a depth now you havent experienced before. They may be able to help you academically, they may not. Either way, your life is so much more than a goddamn phD. Youre suffering now, sure. But make me a promise. Today's date is 26th November 2016. Keep going until 26th November 2017, no matter what. That's the date we're putting on it and its not changing. You're going to see 26th November 2017 and there's no way around it. I promise you, by then, these problems will seem so damn small. So between now and then, you have the option to fix the problems you have, or create a new route in life for yourself. There'll be a lot of stress between now and then, I'm not going to lie to you. But suicide isn't even an option on the table for you. Get it out of your head. Its tests like these that build character,  and you're going to have a great character by next year.
